matchstick.title: V↔X transformation via single stick reposition
matchstick.principle: A V (two diagonal sticks) can become an X (two crossing diagonals) by moving one diagonal stick to intersect the V, and conversely an X can become a V by moving one diagonal away, provided the source remains a valid numeral.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the puzzle involves a V or X and a single stick move could change one into the other to adjust the numeric values.
matchstick.example: Turning V (5) into X (10) adds 5 to the total.

matchstick.title: Check numeric discrepancy to guide stick moves
matchstick.principle: Compute the Arabic values of both sides of the equation; the difference tells how much the total must increase or decrease, guiding which numeral or operator to modify.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Immediately after parsing the Roman numerals, before considering any stick moves.
matchstick.example: If LHS = 15 and RHS = 5, the discrepancy is 10, so a move must change the total by ±10.

matchstick.title: Preserve equality sign integrity
matchstick.principle: The equality sign must remain a valid operator after the move; it cannot be turned into an invalid symbol like '≠', but it may change to another legal operator (e.g., '-' or '+') if a stick is moved to or from it, as long as both resulting operators are valid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: Whenever a stick is taken from or added to the '=' sign; verify that the resulting symbol is still a legal operator.
matchstick.example: Moving one horizontal stick from '=' to a '-' turns the former into '-' and the latter into '=', preserving validity.

matchstick.title: Validate resulting characters after move
matchstick.principle: After relocating a stick, each affected character must still be a recognized Roman numeral or a legal operator; otherwise the move is invalid.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After proposing a stick move, before accepting it as a solution.
matchstick.example: Removing a diagonal from X leaves a single diagonal, which is not a valid numeral, so the move is disallowed.

matchstick.title: Avoid orientation mismatches
matchstick.principle: Sticks keep their orientation; a vertical stick cannot become diagonal, a diagonal cannot become vertical, and a horizontal cannot become diagonal.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When considering moving a stick, ensure the target shape can accept a stick of that orientation.
matchstick.example: A vertical stick cannot be used to form part of an X, which requires diagonals.

matchstick.title: Operator conversion only when resulting operator is valid
matchstick.principle: Changing an operator (e.g., '+' to '-') is allowed only if the new symbol is a legal operator in the context, and the source operator remains valid after the stick is removed; this also covers moving a stick from one operator to another, thereby swapping them.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a stick move involves an operator; verify both the source and target operators stay legal.
matchstick.example: Moving the vertical stick from '+' leaves a '-' and the removed vertical can be placed elsewhere.

matchstick.title: Recompute numeric values after transformation
matchstick.principle: After any stick relocation, recalculate the Arabic values of all numerals and re‑evaluate the arithmetic to check if the equality holds.
matchstick.when_to_apply: After each candidate move, before finalizing the answer.
matchstick.example: After turning '=' into '-', recompute LHS - X = V to verify 5 = 5.

matchstick.title: Plus‑to‑minus conversion via vertical stick relocation
matchstick.principle: A plus sign consists of a vertical and a horizontal stick; moving the vertical stick away turns it into a minus sign, and the removed vertical can be used elsewhere.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the equation contains a '+' and a vertical stick can be moved without breaking the source numeral.
matchstick.example: Changing X + V to X - V by moving the vertical stick from '+' to another character.

matchstick.title: Dual‑character stick relocation for balancing values
matchstick.principle: A single stick can be moved from one character to another, simultaneously decreasing the source’s value and increasing the target’s value, useful for correcting numeric discrepancies.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When the numeric gap can be closed by shifting a stick between two numerals.
matchstick.example: Moving a diagonal from X to V to turn X into V and V into X, adjusting the total by ±5.

matchstick.title: Vertical stick addition creates extra I (value +1)
matchstick.principle: Adding a vertical stick to a numeral creates an additional ‘I’, raising its value by 1 without breaking the original shape.
matchstick.when_to_apply: When a vertical stick is available to be moved and increasing a numeral by 1 would resolve the discrepancy.
matchstick.example: Adding a vertical stick to V to make VI (6).

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model treats sticks as interchangeable symbols, ignoring that diagonal, vertical, and horizontal sticks are distinct.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Enforce orientation constraints: a stick keeps its original orientation when moved.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may think any operator can be altered arbitrarily, including turning '=' into an invalid symbol.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Remember that '=' must remain a valid operator after any move; it cannot become an illegal symbol like '≠'.

matchstick.description: Leaving an invalid character after move
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may remove a stick from a numeral or operator without checking that the remaining shape still represents a legal Roman numeral or operator.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Validate each character after a stick relocation to ensure it matches a known numeral or operator.

matchstick.description: Changing an operator to an invalid shape
matchstick.why_it_happens: The model might add or remove sticks from an operator, producing a symbol that is not '+', '-', or '='.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Check that any operator resulting from a move is one of the allowed symbols.

matchstick.why_it_happens: The model may attempt random stick moves without first understanding how the numeric values differ.
matchstick.how_to_avoid: Compute the Arabic values of both sides early and use the difference to guide which sticks to move.
